clue.text: The actor needing no prompting

parts.note: a player in a silent folk play or mime never speaks a line, so has no use for a prompter feeding forgotten words

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a word-perfect actor; really the performer says nothing at all, keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummer is a performer in traditional mime or folk plays, a silent actor with no lines to forget.

clue.text: Fish stuffing used at sea — a made-up food

indicators.note: the fish is packed inside the word for maritime use, like stuffing in a bird

parts.note: marine means relating to or used at sea
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A recipe of fish stuffing cooked on board ship, offered as an invented dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a manufactured butter substitute, a spread concocted from processed oils rather than churned.

clue.text: One in the eye for Bertie Wooster!

definitions.text: One in the eye for Bertie Wooster!

parts.words: One in the eye for Bertie Wooster!
parts.note: the phrase 'one in the eye' usually means a setback, but here it is literally a single lens worn in one eye, as by P. G. Wodehouse's foppish hero

explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is the comic upper-class narrator of P. G. Wodehouse's Jeeves stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass held in one eye socket, the classic accessory of the upper-class twit Bertie Wooster.

clue.text: Dug up by the roots, and did create a mess

indicators.note: making a mess of the letters jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tore plants out of the ground and left the garden untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a mess' signals the anagram; the first 'a' of that phrase is part of the fodder, while the second word 'mess' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is literally to pull out by the root, from Latin radix, so uprooted plants have been destroyed completely.

clue.text: An end to double parking the wise man accepts

indicators.note: the wise man takes in the other letters, so they sit inside him

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

indicators.note: the parking letter is written twice over

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A sage puts a stop to cars parked two abreast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt or cessation, the point at which something comes to a finish.

clue.text: Hill the counsellor, a most irritating fellow

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
a mentor is a trusted adviser or counsellor

explanation.surface: Introducing Mr Hill, a counsellor who drives everyone up the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torments others is a persistent pest who causes distress and annoyance.

clue.text: Top spread

definitions.meaning: the top of the head, the crown
a savoury paste such as liver paste spread on toast

explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the crown of the head, and pâté is a smooth meat or fish paste for spreading.

clue.text: A couple of beasts in need of sorting out

parts.note: two animals: a nag is a horse
the second animal: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A pair of animals that have got themselves into a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the device itself: a word whose letters are jumbled waits to be sorted into order.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by jumbling another's letters is a puzzle waiting to be rearranged back into sense.

clue.text: Late turn many speak well of

parts.note: ex means former, as in late or ex-husband

indicators.note: turning the word for many makes it read from the other end

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Many people praise a recent performance late on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise lavishly, laud or glorify.

clue.text: Where to find some really husky Europeans

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run that crosses a word break

explanation.surface: A guide to where you might meet tough, gravel-voiced Continentals.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is concealed in husKY Europeans; 'husky' tempts thoughts of sled dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a Scottish island of the Inner Hebrides, a place one can go looking for things.

clue.text: To search a bag is in order

indicators.note: the bag word is placed inside the order word

parts.note: rank is an order or row, as in rank and file
a sac is a bag-like pouch in a plant or animal

explanation.surface: Looking through a handbag is perfectly acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in order' reads as approval; it is a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly and roughly, turning everything over.

clue.text: Withdraw both note and pamphlet

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tract is a short pamphlet, typically religious or political

explanation.surface: Pulling back both a musical note and a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or recant.

clue.text: She'd displace an American eccentric, a well-known scientist

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are set out of their usual order
the two letters of the clue word an are pushed out of the word American

explanation.surface: A woman would oust an odd American, a famous scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displace' removes AN from AMERICAN to leave AMERIC; 'eccentric' then jumbles SHED with AMERIC. Displacement is also the scientist's famous bath-time discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mathematician of Syracuse who discovered the principle of buoyancy and shouted Eureka.

clue.text: A trainee after gold, it's said

indicators.note: the article and the trainee come after the gold in the answer

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee athlete going after a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes what is spoken rather than written, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: "Be not too tame neither, but let your own — be your tutor." (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Be not too tame neither, but let your own — be your tutor." (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Be not too tame neither, but let your own — be your tutor." (Hamlet)
parts.note: Hamlet's advice to the players: the missing word is the quality of good judgement the actors should let guide them

explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is good judgement and tact, the faculty Hamlet tells the players to follow.

clue.text: The country in which one hundred have a quarter of the territory

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass
land means territory

explanation.surface: A nation where a hundred people hold a quarter of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Titled people subjected to the underworld make allowances

indicators.note: in a down clue, being subject to something puts the titled people beneath it

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
counts are noblemen with a title

explanation.surface: Aristocrats in the grip of organised crime make concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the underworld' suggests gangsters; it is Dis, the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounts are reductions in price, and discounting is allowing for something, as in making allowance for exaggeration.

clue.text: The person attempting to get outside decoration smarter

indicators.note: the one trying wraps around the medal letters, putting them inside

parts.note: a trier is someone who tries or attempts
MM is the Military Medal, a British gallantry decoration

explanation.surface: Someone trying to step outside to admire a smarter ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: MM stands for Military Medal, a British army award for bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmer is the comparative of trim, meaning neater or more smartly turned out.

clue.text: Twisted and turned when quite unnecessary

indicators.note: twisted means wrenched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone twisted and turned when there was no need to.
explanation.definitionFit: Redundant means superfluous, no longer needed.

clue.text: Not stopping to put thoughts into words

definitions.meaning: a non-stop train or delivery that runs straight through
to state or voice what one thinks

explanation.definitionFit: An express train makes no intermediate halts, and to express something is to articulate it in speech.

clue.text: Step over a plant — that's the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, the step sits above the plant

parts.note: pas is a step in ballet, French for step
sage is an aromatic herb

explanation.surface: Stride across a plant and you have found the route.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a corridor or route, a way through.

clue.text: The name of the cleaner taken in free

indicators.note: the cleaner is taken inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A cleaner's name is recorded on being hired for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is old British slang for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is a common man's given name.

clue.text: High-ranking officer causing a new lad to edge back inside

indicators.note: the reversed edge is placed within the reworked lad
new means made afresh, so the letters of lad are reformed
back means the edge word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A senior officer makes a young lad retreat into the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LAD into DAL; 'back' turns RIM into MIR, which goes inside DAL after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a naval officer of the highest rank, commanding a fleet.

clue.text: The chest for instance

definitions.meaning: a chest is a large box or trunk

explanation.definitionFit: A case is a box or container, and also an example or occurrence of something.

clue.text: Shy egg-head group

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A timid intellectual belongs to a particular set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, but here it is the verb to throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class or group, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: Travel, being an artisan

parts.note: a journey is an act of travel
man is a human being

explanation.surface: A craftsman explaining that he is on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a skilled tradesman who has finished an apprenticeship and works for an employer.

clue.text: Cotton on to this for a dance!

definitions.meaning: a spool around which cotton thread is wound
a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance

explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a bobbin for thread, and also a brisk folk dance.

clue.text: He'll give an account of himself

definitions.text: He'll give an account of himself

parts.words: He'll give an account of himself
parts.note: a man's name that is also a word for an invoice or account, so the person is the account

explanation.walkthrough: 'give an account of himself' usually means to explain one's conduct; here the man literally is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is an itemised account of charges, and Bill is a man's name.

clue.text: Tots in a specially designed place

indicators.note: the letters are laid out to a new design

explanation.surface: Toddlers housed in a purpose-built nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a post or place where someone is stationed.

clue.text: Bore returning with soldiers to a North African area

indicators.note: returning means the word for bore is read backwards

parts.note: to tire is to bore or weary
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A tedious veteran comes home with troops to a part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses TIRE to give ERIT. Strictly Eritrea lies in north-east Africa, on the Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: 2 down for example absorbing the old-fashioned girl

indicators.note: the example letters take in the archaic word, which sits inside them

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
ye is an archaic spelling of the
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A monocle, say, catches sight of a girl in vintage dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single lens worn in the eye, a kind of eyepiece.

clue.text: Is seen hanging around a low joint

definitions.text: Is seen hanging around a low joint

parts.words: Is seen hanging around a low joint
parts.note: suggests a loiterer at a seedy bar, but describes jewellery worn around the lowest joint of the leg

explanation.walkthrough: A 'low joint' sounds like a dive bar; it is the ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is an ornamental band or chain worn round the ankle.
